# `js/jsdoc-informative-docs`

**JSDoc text that adds something to the name it documents**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `useless_words`, `excluded_tags` |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (what the comment should say is the author's) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-jsdoc/informative-docs` |

## What it checks

A block's description, and a tag's description, says something the documented name does not: text whose every word is one of the name's words, or one of `a`, `an`, `i`, `in`, `of`, `s`, `the` (the plugin's default useless words), is reported — `/** The name. */` on `name`, `@param name the name`. Words are compared in lower case after splitting at case changes (`getUserName` is `get`, `user`, `name`); `an` and `our` count as `a`. The names are the identifiers of the code the block documents: the declaration, a method's class too, a variable's initializer. The plugin's `aliases`, `uselessWords` and `excludedTags` options are built as `useless_words` and `excluded_tags`; `aliases` is not.

**Why:** A comment that only repeats the name adds noise, and its presence makes a reader think the thing is documented.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `useless_words` | `string[]` | `["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"]` | words ignored when looking for one that adds meaning |
| `excluded_tags` | `string[]` | `[]` | tags whose description is not checked |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-informative-docs"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/jsdoc-informative-docs".options]
useless_words = ["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"]
excluded_tags = []
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = { severity = "error", options = { useless_words = ["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"], excluded_tags = ["param"] } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `useless_words`

*string[]* · default `["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"]`

words ignored when looking for one that adds meaning

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-informative-docs".options]
useless_words = ["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"]
```

#### `excluded_tags`

*string[]* · default `[]`

tags whose description is not checked

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-informative-docs".options]
excluded_tags = ["param"]
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/jsdoc-informative-docs.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### excluded_tags

```toml
[rules."js/jsdoc-informative-docs".options]
excluded_tags = ["param"]
```

```js
/**
 * Greets someone.
 * @param {string} name the name
 */
function greet(name) {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = { options = { useless_words = ["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"] } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/jsdoc-informative-docs" = { severity = "warn", options = { useless_words = ["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"] } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/jsdoc-informative-docs": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"useless_words": ["a", "an", "i", "in", "of", "s", "the"]}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-informative-docs: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/jsdoc-informative-docs expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/jsdoc-informative-docs --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/jsdoc-informative-docs       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/jsdoc-informative-docs  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>             # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Say what the name does not: why it exists, what it returns, a unit, a constraint — or delete the comment.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
/**
 * The user name.
 * @param {string} userName the user name
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

#### Do

```js
/**
 * Renames the signed-in account.
 * @param {string} userName the new display name, at most 40 characters
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
/**
 * The user name.
 * @param {string} userName the user name
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

#### Do

```jsx
/**
 * Renames the signed-in account.
 * @param {string} userName the new display name, at most 40 characters
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
/**
 * The user name.
 * @param {string} userName the user name
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

#### Do

```ts
/**
 * Renames the signed-in account.
 * @param {string} userName the new display name, at most 40 characters
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
/**
 * The user name.
 * @param {string} userName the user name
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```

#### Do

```tsx
/**
 * Renames the signed-in account.
 * @param {string} userName the new display name, at most 40 characters
 */
function setUserName(userName) {}
```
